payload.mechanism: PRIMARY claim path uses the row own dispatch_lane field, frozen at the ORIGINAL promote time, without re-validating it against the row CURRENT next_agent -- a multi-hop supervised+plan_only chain (e.g. ba->architect) that cycles back through ready[] for its 2nd hop keeps the STALE 1st-hop dispatch_lane, causing SLS to re-dispatch the wrong (already-completed) agent on its next claim.
payload.live_incident: FIX-BCTC-NEWSCHAIN-FALLBACK-ZEROS-WRITE-TARGET: promoted_at=2026-08-07T19:21:36Z stamped dispatch_lane=ba; ba completed at 20:34:58Z (ba_spec_complete=true, ba_handoff=docs/handoffs/FIX-BCTC-NEWSCHAIN-FALLBACK-ZEROS-WRITE-TARGET-BA-spec.md, commit bdaeddb3b) and correctly updated the row own next_agent field to architect, but the row cycled back to ready[] for its next hop; SLS claim at 21:52:22Z used the frozen dispatch_lane=ba instead of the row live next_agent=architect, which would have re-spawned ba on already-finished work had dev-team not caught it via RAW cross-check against ba_completed_at/ba_handoff before dispatching.
payload.workaround_applied_this_tick: dev-team corrected dispatch_lane + head.next_agent to architect in-place via orch-apply.sh before spawning; did not re-run ba.
payload.suggested_fix: PRIMARY claim path should re-resolve dispatch_lane at claim time (same resolved_dispatch_lane($detail_items) helper the FALLBACK path already uses) whenever the row live next_agent differs from the stamped dispatch_lane -- or simpler: PRIMARY should prefer effective_next_agent over the stale dispatch_lane stamp when they disagree, since next_agent is the more current source of truth once a row has already completed at least one prior dispatch hop.
